title: Bulk Write Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and main trade-off of bulk write operations.

Verify the expected result, one edge case, and the relevant version/deployment assumption.

content.intro: Learn bulk write operations as part of Updates, Deletes and Bulk Operations. The lesson preserves the PDF subtopics, connects them to a practical MongoDB pattern, and ends with a verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Bulk Write Operations is a query or write-building block. Construct a narrow filter, predict the documents that should match, choose only the fields needed, and verify matched or modified counts before relying on a mutation.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the behavior you want, identify the collection/document shape and access pattern involved, then select the smallest MongoDB operation that expresses the requirement. Run a read-only find with the same filter first and review the returned identifiers before mutating data.

content_blocks.expected_output: The bulk result summarizes the attempted operations; inspect write errors and the counts rather than treating partial failure as total success.
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf displays this example as a reference and does not execute a MongoDB server or arbitrary driver code in the page. Run shell examples with mongosh, or driver examples in a separately configured Node.js/Python lab, against a disposable database. Verify installed server/driver versions and deployment feature availability first. Never place credentials in source files.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a dedicated training database and synthetic fixtures. Remove only objects created by this lesson or recreate the disposable database after confirming the target; do not run destructive/reset commands against production.

content_blocks.title: Environment and safety note
content_blocks.text: All examples are teaching references, not production-ready configuration. MongoDB Atlas-specific Search, Vector Search, monitoring, backup and automation features are marked as deployment-dependent. Server, driver, shell and managed-service capabilities differ; check the official documentation that matches your target.

content.task: Try it yourself: Use a selective filter and the narrowest update operator that expresses the intended change; verify matched/modified counts and test an idempotent retry where applicable. Submit your choice plus the expected result/evidence and one edge case.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a broad or incorrect filter
common_mistakes.why: A filter may match more documents than expected, especially when missing fields, arrays or implicit AND conditions are involved.
common_mistakes.fix: Run a read-only find with the same filter first and review the returned identifiers before mutating data.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a static reference result proves the environment will behave identically.
common_mistakes.why: MongoDB server, shell, driver, managed service and permissions can affect the available behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the target versions and privileges, run the smallest safe test, and keep expected and actual results side by side.
